messages:
maya: Heads up — CI started flagging nondet failures for the quantized bring-up. Failing tests are sampling-based evals (top_p/temp combos). :eyes:

ton y: which job? link?

maya: https://ci.internal/reds/6421 — happens on shard 12 and 19 intermittently. locally can't repro after 20 runs. CI shows different token-level distributions across runs.

sasha: quick guess: worker reuse + seed assignment race. saw something similar when the pool reaped and respawned.

maya: i dumped a few logs:
```
RUN=6421 SHARD=12 worker_id=3 seed_env=unset seed_assigned=0x5f37a1
sampling_params: {"top_p":0.93, "temperature":0.8}
sample_counts: runA: [14,3,2,...] runB: [12,5,2,...]
```

maya: note: sometimes seed_assigned is identical across two workers in same run.

ton y: hmm — eval-runner should be calling rng = RandomState(base_seed + shard_id + pid) not base_seed alone. is that new resume code path using monotonic timestamp?

sasha: exact. the resume path (_hot_start_) was left using global entropy_source() which returns monotonic microseconds. When two workers start in same millisecond they get same seed -> "coalescence".

devon: repro steps? i can spin a local docker that mimics the CI shard scheduler.

maya: repro is noisy but this script shows it quickly:
```python
for i in range(200):
    spawn_workers(4, start_fn=lambda wid: rng_init(entropy_source() + wid))
    record(seeds)
```

maya: you can see repeated seeds across workers for some iterations.

ton y: quick patch idea: prefer deterministic derivation from job_id+shard+worker_idx and only use entropy_source for initial job seed, not per-worker.

sasha: agreed. also top_p combined with quantized logits seems to amplify differences — one-token shift cascades. so a seed collision that flips one early token makes the whole distribution look different.

eval-bot: CI note: rerun #6421 triggered. Artifacts: https://ci.internal/reds/6421/artifacts/seed-dumps.tar.gz

devon: i'll prototype a fix: deterministic seeding + small change in resume to rederive per-worker seeds using HKDF(job_seed, info=worker_id). will run against CI sharded schedule.

maya: thanks. also add a regression test: run few short epochs with forced simultaneous worker spawns to catch coalescence.

ton y: and add a metric in dashboard: "seed-entropy-per-worker" and an alert if collision rate > 0.1% across a job.

sasha: low-effort mitigation: on startup, if seed collision detected, increment by worker_id until unique — cheap stopgap.

devon: i'll push an RFC branch today and attach to PR. cc @sasha @maya for review.

maya: perfect. once fixed we'll re-run the quantized benchmark to see if the CI flakiness disappears.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from tony)
